thread:
alex: Heads-up — saw a tailing perf crossover on the Flash/SDPA chooser during a canary. Causal requests at seqlen~256 with head_dim=22 jump ~35% slower than non-causal path. repro attached.
priya: Ugh. Which runtime and GPU? sm86 or sm90?
sasha: sm86, runtime v2.4.1, model=redwood-generate-7b-lite, batch=1, microbatching off. repro script below.
alex: ```bash
# repro loop
python perf_probe.py --model rgen7b --seqlen 256 --head-dim 22 --causal true --gpu sm86
```
logs:
alex: ```
[2026-03-01 12:02:10] kernel_picker: chose flash_v3 for non-causal
[2026-03-01 12:02:10] kernel_picker: probed sdpa_slowpath for causal, fallback to flash_v2
[2026-03-01 12:02:10] runtime: kv-cache warmup hit=0 miss=12
[2026-03-01 12:02:10] perf: 14.2 ms/token (non-causal) vs 19.1 ms/token (causal)
```
morgan: Interesting that kv-cache warmup misses correlate. Could be that the causal path forces a different kernel that doesn't use the same prefetch/warmup sequence.
jen: Can you paste the kernel probe output? We added a microprobe in kernel_picker recently.
sasha: Here — probe trace (trimmed): ```
probe: head_dim=22 seqlen=256 -> tried flash_v3 (skipped: causal incompatible)
probe: tried flash_v2 (est_lat=13.8ms)
probe: tried sdpa_unrolled (est_lat=14.0ms, but hw_gen=sm86 unoptimized)
chosen: flash_v2 hysteresis=0.2
```
priya: Ah, flash_v3 being marked "causal incompatible" is suspicious — v3 has causal support but our compatibility table might be overly strict for head_dim not divisible by 8.
alex: Exactly. It looks like the compatibility check rejects v3 for head_dim%8!=0 on sm86, even though it can run with a small padding path. That causes fallback to v2 which is slower for this seqlen.
morgan: That aligns with the warmup miss: v3 path would do a different KV layout and reuse prefetched tiles; v2 does per-token ops and thrashes L2.
jen: Two short experiments:
- relax v3 compatibility to allow head_dim%2==0 (soft allow) and add runtime pad to 8 for dispatch
- add a warmup sequence before measuring (send 4 initial dummy tokens to populate KV cache)
priya: I can run the first experiment on a canary. If we auto-pad at dispatch we should also ensure memory accounting for kv cache indexes.
sasha: Also propose adding a seq-length bucket edge at 192/256 in picker; currently buckets are 128/512 so the 256 case sits in big bucket that biases away from v3.
alex: Good call. Bucket granularity might be too coarse: refunding microbench shows v3 wins for 192-320 range on sm86 when allowed.
ops-bot: Deploy plan check: patch must go to runtime branch w/ perf test, add unit for head-dim compatibility, and flag to opt-out per-customer.
jen: For canary steps:
1) priya toggle compat flag + auto-pad dispatch on canary nodes (2 GPUs)
2) run repro and collect token-level latencies + KV warmup stats
3) if stable <5% regression, roll to beta
alex: I'll add a small probe harness: send 8 warmup tokens then measure 100 tokens, record kv_hit_rate and per-token latency buckets.
sasha: One more wrinkle — when batch>1 we see the opposite: v2 wins at batch=4 because its multistream kernel packs better. Need to capture that in policy: route by (seqlen, head_dim, batch).
priya: Agreed. I'll run a small grid over batch in {1,2,4}, seqlen in {128,192,256,320}, head_dim in {16,22,32,64} and post results to perf board.
morgan: If the grid is big, we can populate a compact lookup table and then train a tiny regressor to interpolate picks for unseen combos.
jen: For immediate mitigation, can we add a short-term override: if causal && head_dim in {22,30,46} && seqlen in [192,320] prefer flash_v3 with pad? That would cover the canary regressions.
alex: I'll prepare the override PR and a rollback flag. Also adding telemetry events: kernel_choice, kv_warmup_hits, seqlen, head_dim, batch.
sasha: Nice. One ask: mark the compatibility doc where we list "causal incompatible" reasons; it's getting out of sync with real kernels.
ops-bot: Reminder: create a follow-up ticket for regression test in CI with sm86 variants.
priya: Running first canary now, will post results in ~12m.
alex: thanks — @priya :thumbsup:
priya: quick update: after enabling soft-allow+pad, causal latency dropped to 14.8 ms/token and kv_warmup_hits went from 0 to 9/12. Still slightly behind non-causal but within noise.
jen: That's promising. Keep the canary running for 2h, then we'll run batch grid.
alex: Filing notes in perf board and will link the PR.
